summary: The study investigates the use of copper(I)-N,N0-di-sec-butylacetamidinate as a precursor for atomic layer deposition (ALD) of copper on nickel surfaces. The process involves thermal activation and dissociative adsorption of the precursor, with optimal deposition occurring between 350-450 K. The study highlights the importance of hydrogen in the ALD process and the need for stable organic intermediates to ensure clean deposition.
evidence: The adsorption and thermal activation of copper(I)-N,N0-di-sec-butylacetamidinate on a Ni(110) single-crystal surface were characterized in connection with the use of that compound as a precursor for the growth of copper films via atomic layer deposition (ALD) processes. A temperature window between approximately 350 and 450 K was identified for the clean deposition of the precursor on the surface.
